result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A has a proportionate review step that singles out firing and safety content. Unlike B, it also says when a page goes stale and who watches for that, which is part of rubric item 3. B is tighter and has clearer fill-in placeholders, but it gives pricing and stock to Tobias without support from the facts, has a 'Cone 6' example title, and has no way to spot outdated pages. A probably runs a little over 800 words. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B covers more of what the request asked for. It gives clear rules for when a page is out of date (reformulation, price change, retest), names who watches for them, and puts Ines's firing and safety checks in source tables. A is tighter and closer to the word target, but it has no way to tell when a page is stale. Its 'Cone 6' example title also slips in a firing value the shop never gave. B runs over 800 words and adds a 3-day review deadline and a price/stock owner that the shop didn't state.
